title: [Advanced Paste] - Media transcoding truncates filenames with multiple periods
author: carmatos

confidence.rationale: The filename loss is directly explained by the current output-path code and needs no additional reporter evidence.

judgment.rationale: The issue’s reproduction maps exactly onto a localized bug in Advanced Paste transcoding: the code strips one extension with Path.GetFileNameWithoutExtension and then strips the remaining suffix again by passing the already-trimmed base name through Path.ChangeExtension. That makes this a strong candidate for a full implementation-grade design.
evidence: The issue reproduces with filenames like some.video.mov and some.audio.wav and reports outputs some.mp4 and some.mp3.
TranscodeHelpers.TranscodeMediaAsync sets inputFileNameWithoutExtension = Path.GetFileNameWithoutExtension(inputFile.Path), which yields “some.video” for some.video.mov.
The next line builds outputFilePath with Path.ChangeExtension(outputFileName, extension), which treats “.video” as an extension and truncates the remaining segment again.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve the full design to preserve multi-dot base names when Advanced Paste writes transcoded output files.

fix_assessment.rationale: No existing fix attempt is linked, and the defect is directly localizable to current Advanced Paste output-name construction.

proposed_fixes.title: Preserve every base-name segment when building transcoded output filenames
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Advanced Paste strips the original extension once and then calls Path.ChangeExtension on the already-trimmed base name, which interprets the remaining final segment as another extension and drops it.
plan: Build the output leaf name from inputFile.Name, not Path.ChangeExtension on an already-processed stem.
Append the target extension directly and keep the existing _1 collision behavior only for same-extension transcodes.
Add automated coverage for multi-dot filenames and same-extension collision naming.
verification: some.video.mp4 transcoded to mp4 still uses a non-clobbering name such as some.video_1.mp4

confidence.rationale: The current code deterministically produces the truncation described by the issue.

issue_context.summary: Advanced Paste’s media transcoding path drops everything after the first period in the base filename because it strips the output stem twice.
known_information: The issue is open, unassigned, and labeled Issue-Bug / Needs-Triage.
The report gives a deterministic reproduction using filenames like some.video.mov and some.audio.wav.
No comments, attachments, or competing fix work are present.
inferences: This is a deterministic filename-construction bug, not a codec or shell-integration problem.
issue_context.analysis: This is one of the two best actionable bugs in the batch for a full design: single owning method, obvious expected behavior, and straightforward regression coverage.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the complete issue body and current labels.
Inspected src/modules/AdvancedPaste/AdvancedPaste/Helpers/TranscodeHelpers.cs and the existing transcode integration tests.
Checked file history for TranscodeHelpers.cs and confirmed the bug descends from the original transcode implementation.

design.root_cause: TranscodeHelpers.TranscodeMediaAsync constructs output filenames by first stripping the original file extension with Path.GetFileNameWithoutExtension and then calling Path.ChangeExtension on that partially processed base name. For multi-dot names, the second call drops the remaining suffix segment (for example some.video -> some.mp4).
evidence: Issue reproduction: some.video.mov produces some.mp4 instead of some.video.mp4.
Current code at TranscodeHelpers.cs lines 40-53 computes inputFileNameWithoutExtension from the full input path and then passes outputFileName through Path.ChangeExtension.
Path.ChangeExtension on the already-trimmed string treats the remaining trailing segment as an extension, which exactly explains the truncation.

affected_files.purpose: Owns the transcoded output file-name and output-path construction.
Add deterministic filename-shape regression tests without requiring external media test assets.
Optional integration assertion that the emitted StorageFile name matches the deterministic helper behavior during real transcoding.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The method derives inputFileNameWithoutExtension with Path.GetFileNameWithoutExtension(inputFile.Path), optionally adds _1, and then calls Path.ChangeExtension(outputFileName, extension) before creating the output file.
implementation_steps.change: Extract deterministic output-leaf-name construction that operates on inputFile.Name, preserves every base-name segment before the original extension, and appends the target extension directly instead of routing the already-trimmed stem through Path.ChangeExtension.
edge_cases: Keep same-extension collision naming by inserting _1 before the final target extension.
Use inputFile.Name rather than inputFile.Path for name math so directory segments never participate in extension stripping.
tests: Deterministic helper/unit test for multi-dot stems and same-extension naming.
Real transcode integration check that outputFile.Name matches the helper result.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: There is no focused automated test that locks the transcode output filename logic independently of the media transcoder runtime.
implementation_steps.change: Add a small unit-test surface (or extract an internal helper) so naming can be verified with pure filename inputs such as some.video.mov and some.audio.wav.
edge_cases: Cover filenames with only one dot to keep previous behavior unchanged.
tests: Three deterministic filename cases from the issue and the same-extension collision case.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The integration test validates media properties but does not assert the emitted output filename shape.
implementation_steps.change: When the optional transcode test assets exist, assert that the output StorageFile name matches the new deterministic helper so multi-dot filenames are covered end-to-end.
edge_cases: Keep the existing Assert.Inconclusive behavior when local media asset folders are absent.
tests: End-to-end mp3 and mp4 transcode name assertions for representative multi-dot assets when the optional test folder is present.

verify: Run the deterministic Advanced Paste unit tests covering multi-dot stems.
Run the existing transcode integration tests when local media assets are available.
Manually transcode representative files such as some.video.mov and some.audio.wav and confirm output names preserve the full stem.
risks: If the same-extension collision case is handled incorrectly, output files could overwrite or duplicate unexpected names.
Touching filename construction in only one branch could make mp3 and mp4 behavior diverge.
alternatives: Keep Path.ChangeExtension and try to escape multi-dot stems. Rejected because the problem is using ChangeExtension on an already processed stem at all.
Always append the target extension to the full original filename. Rejected because it would produce names like some.video.mov.mp4 instead of replacing the original extension.

actions.label: Approve multi-dot transcode filename fix
actions.note: This is a small, well-bounded Advanced Paste bug with implementation-ready design detail.
